author: CNN
description:
As the summit last week demonstrated, Presidents Donald Trump and Xi Jinping are searching for ways to work together despite the growing rivalry between the two countries.

They might take a look at a striking, somewhat unnoticed case of quiet cooperation involving American and Chinese technologies. By now, the world has heard about the Hugging Face attack in July, in which OpenAI agents broke into Hugging Face, a leading American AI platform. Hugging Face couldn’t find an American AI model able to investigate, but a Chinese model could.

CNN’s Fareed Zakaria gives his take on the ways China and the US are better served by a relationship of managed interdependence rather than weaponized interdependence. Also, Fareed talks to Finnish President Alexander Stubb & Jonas Gahr Støre, the Norwegian Prime Minister on Europe’s view of the war in Ukraine and if Europe can keep up it’s support for Ukraine.

title: Why China & US actually need each other | Fareed’s Take

author: CNN
description:
Prosecutors in New York are reopening an investigation into an alleged gang rape of a former Cornell University student after a civil lawsuit was filed earlier this month by the woman’s lawyer, claiming the school did not do enough to protect the accuser.

Tompkins County District Attorney Matthew Van Houten told ABC his office plans to present the case to a grand jury after the original investigation into the alleged 2024 assault resulted in no criminal charges. Van Houten said the allegations in the civil complaint were “dramatically different” than the woman’s statement to police two years ago, at the time of the alleged incident.

The disturbing allegations about the assault of the former student, identified as Jane Doe, have already sparked widespread criticism and again put a spotlight on how universities handle student claims of sexual assault.

1:52 DA's statement on why no charges were filed in 2024

description:
UPDATE: The five men arrested on suspicion of a plot to attack a UK airbase used by long-range US bombers are to be released on bail, British counter-terrorism police said on Monday. The five are all British nationals from the London area, aged between 23 and 25, according to police. The release of the men does not mean that the investigation is over, Laurence Taylor, a senior officer in the UK counter-terrorism police said at a brief news conference Monday. The five men would be subject to stringent conditions on their movements, he said.

------------------------------

British police on Sunday arrested five men on suspicion of terror and explosives offenses close to an airbase in England that is used by US long-range bombers in the war against Iran.
